_instructions: EMPTY TEMPLATE — the code does NOT read this file: it reads 'vocabulary.json' (without .example).
Usage: copy this file to vocabulary.json and fill that one in. vocabulary.json is gitignored,
so your values stay on your machine and a 'git pull' never overwrites them.
If vocabulary.json is missing the pipeline still runs: it skips catch-phrase
detection, but acoustic detection (Cinema Engine) and base scoring keep working.
Keys starting with '_' are ignored by the loader: use them for your own notes.
The values below are EMPTY on purpose. Examples live in the _help field of each section.

_help: Who you are. Used to build the prompt of the AI agent that picks the final clips.
name            : your name/handle, as you want it to appear in the prompt
genres          : your genres (e.g. ["horror", "soulslike"])
description     : your style in a few words (e.g. "authentic, ironic, reactive")
selection_notes : extra rules for the AI, one per line (e.g. "drop the chat about exams and films")
If you leave everything empty the AI still works, but it knows nothing about your style.
Hint passed to Whisper so it transcribes proper nouns, jargon and catch-phrases
better — otherwise it invents them (the classic: a shouted catch-phrase becomes a
word that merely sounds like it).
vod  : used on the full VOD transcript
clip : shorter version, used when Whisper re-runs on the individual cuts
Keep them SHORT. Very long sentences make transcription worse, not better.
Your key phrases. The code uses them in three ways:
phrases          -> merges nearby segments and anchors the cut on the big moment
words            -> like phrases, but on single words (exact match, not substring:
so "go" does not fire inside "prego")
absolute_phrases -> the 'iconic' subset: recovers a highlight even if the AI
rejected it, and is the last safety net of the selection
Rule: phrases and absolute_phrases are multi-word expressions, all lowercase.
words are single tokens.
Example phrases: ["a nanna", "porco trollo"] — words: ["nanna", "sium"]
These get fed to the agent and to the merge: do NOT put generic swearing here,
or a clip will fire every two minutes.
Words that score segments. Each category weighs differently:
god_tier -> maximum bonus: the moment that is a Short on its own
shock    -> astonishment, disbelief
panic    -> fear, urgency (horror)
clutch   -> a feat, a win, 'we made it'
lore     -> reflection, discovery, explanation
All lowercase. Phrases of 3 characters or less require a whole-word match.
Note: these are the words of YOUR way of streaming. The text below is
only a generic example, replace it with your own.
Corrections applied to the text BEFORE scoring.
Key: a regular expression (regex). Value: how it should be written on screen.
Fixes what Whisper mishears in your catch-phrases.
Example: {"(?i)\\b(ah\\s+)?nanna\\b": "A nanna!"}
